A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GUI-AIMA and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite reformatting, merged tables, and relocated analyses.

before.justification: v3 reports original GUI-AIMA benchmark accuracies, component ablations, convergence measurements, inference timings, and attention-head analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds InternVL3.5 experiments, Gaussian-label sensitivity results, controlled computational measurements, and failure examples.

M1.justification: v4 adds an InternVL3.5-specific adaptation that maps visual patch indices back to spatial coordinates under dynamic image tiling (Section 4.3). The core anchor aggregation, head weighting, supervision, and two-step inference remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation coverage remain unchanged, including ScreenSpot-v1/v2/Pro, OSWorld-G, UI-Vision, and MMBench-GUI-L2. The new backbone experiments and Word failure examples remain within the existing GUI-grounding tasks and domains.

E2.justification: v4 adds unadapted InternVL3.5-2B and -4B comparators in Table 7 and autoregressive anchor-sequence and coordinate-generation controls in Table 5. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Existing training budgets, data selections, and grounding metrics are retained. Added protocols include InternVL3.5 experiments using the 45k ablation data, an alpha sweep from 0.6 to 1.0, and single-/two-step latency and maximum-memory measurements with a matched-output autoregressive control.

E4.justification: v4 substantially broadens validation through cross-backbone testing, Gaussian-label sensitivity, controlled attention-extraction overhead comparisons, and concrete interaction failures (Tables 5–7 and Appendix H). The earlier attention-head pruning analysis is retained in Appendix C, rather than removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the empirical comparisons. The new experiments do not introduce these practices.

E6.justification: All ten retained tables have unchanged numerical results, but v4 adds distinct findings on backbone generality, sensitivity, computational costs, and failures. New Table 7 reports overall accuracy of 39.8 versus 45.5 for InternVL3.5-2B versus its GUI-AIMA adaptation, and 45.7 versus 48.4 for 4B. Table 5 adds latency/memory measurements, including 778.5 ms/10.69 GB for partial eager attention versus 4548.1 ms/24.75 GB for full eager attention.

T1.justification: The attention definitions, aggregation equations, visual-sink selection, Gaussian labels, KL objective, and extraction-complexity argument are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions, data-efficiency claims, and headline benchmark accuracies. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining their core scope.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly discusses the latency-versus-memory tradeoff relative to coordinate generation and interprets the new experiments as supporting backbone generality and alpha selection. Appendix H adds specific limitations involving an inactive control behind a dialog and an incorrect prerequisite-action order.

D1.justification: v4 specifies an NVIDIA A6000 for the new overhead measurements, explains the matched anchor-output control, and describes the InternVL3.5 spatial-remapping adaptation. Existing training hardware, hyperparameters, crop settings, anchor implementation details, and project access information remain available.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Anticipatory Planning for Multimodal AI Agents and InternVL3.5. The substantive positioning against TAG, GUI-Actor, and coordinate-based grounding remains unchanged; consolidated duplicate references do not represent removed research.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative are retained. Changes include local wording edits, inline enumeration of contributions, updated author notes, acknowledgements, and relocation of Section 4.5 to Appendix C with corresponding appendix reorganization.

P2.justification: v4 extensively restyles typography, margins, headings, and display placement. It merges v3 Tables 2 and 3 into substantially smaller side-by-side Tables 2a–b, relocates and enlarges Figure 6, and adds Tables 5–7 and Figure 11. Existing figures otherwise retain their content.

improvement.justification: v4 provides useful evidence for previously untested backbone generality, checks the Gaussian-label parameter, isolates computational overhead, and documents concrete failure modes. These additions improve validation and transparency while the established results remain intact. The much smaller merged benchmark tables reduce readability, partly offsetting the gains.
